1) Fundus albipunctatus — Most likely. Lifelong, non‑progressive nyctalopia + few yellow/white flecks on fundus and ERG pattern of essentially absent rod responses initially with large, slow scotopic responses after prolonged dark adaptation is classic. Recommended confirmatory tests: dark‑adaptation curve testing, fundus autofluorescence/OCT to characterize flecks, and RDH5 (or other retinoid‑cycle gene) genetic testing.

2) Oguchi disease — Second most likely. Also a congenital stationary nyctalopia with markedly reduced rod ERG that can recover after prolonged dark adaptation; characteristic Mizuo–Nakamura fundus sheen may explain the indistinct grayish circle. Confirm with light/dark serial fundus photography to look for reversible fundus sheen and SAG/GRK1 genetic testing.

3) Complete congenital stationary night blindness (cCSNB) — Possible. Presents with lifelong night blindness and an electronegative flash ERG (absent/markedly reduced b‑wave) with otherwise relatively preserved fundus; less favored because of fundus flecks and clear recovery after prolonged dark adaptation. Confirm with careful ERG waveform review (a‑ vs b‑wave), genetic testing (e.g., NYX, GRM6).

4) Retinitis punctata albescens (a fleck dystrophy / early flecked RP variant) — Less likely but possible. Flecks on fundus and rod dysfunction; tends to be progressive with peripheral field loss over time (not currently present). Confirm with serial visual fields, FAF/OCT, and genetic testing (eg RLBP1), and longitudinal ERG monitoring.

5) Chronic vitamin A deficiency (or other acquired hypovitaminosis A) — Least likely given childhood onset and stability, but can produce night blindness and low rod ERG which may improve with repletion. Check serum retinol level and dietary history; consider therapeutic trial if low.

Suggested next practical steps (to confirm and guide management)
- Formal dark‑adaptometry (document rod recovery curve) and repeat ffERG with clearly documented pre‑ and post‑prolonged dark adaptation tracings.
- Fundus autofluorescence and macular/retinal OCT; serial color photos including after prolonged dark adaptation (for Mizuo sign).
- Targeted genetic testing panel for inherited stationary night blindness / fleck disorders (RDH5, RLBP1, SAG, GRK1, NYX, CACNA1F, etc.).
- Serum vitamin A (retinol) level if dietary risk factors present.
